headline: Review of school opening, special education program review, and service requirement at Westbrook High School.
summary: The meeting will cover the opening of school, including the cell phone ban at Westbrook High School, Pre K, and SIOP. It will also cover a special education program review, a service requirement at Westbrook High School, and goals for the year.

SIOP
 
in
 
Westbrook
 
 
The
 
Sheltered
 
Instruction
 
Observation
 
Protocol
 
(SIOP
 
Model)
 
is
 
a
 
research-based
 
instructional
 
framework
 
designed
 
to
 
help
 
educators
 
integrate
 
academic
 
language
 
development
 
with
 
grade-level
 
content
 
mastery.
 
While
 
created
 
to
 
directly
 
support
 
students
 
developing
 
English
 
language
 
proficiency,
 
all
 
learners
 
benefit
 
from
 
this
 
model
  
by
 
providing
 
instructional
 
practices
 
that
 
support
 
language
 
and
 
literacy
 
in
 
all
 
grade
 
levels,
 
among
 
all
 
students,
 
across
 
all
 
content
 
areas.
  
It
 
targets
 
content
 
and
 
language
 
objectives
 
as
 
a
 
foundation
 
for
 
all
 
learning.
 
SIOP
 
was
 
developed
 
by
 
Drs.
 
Jana
 
Echevarria,
 
Mary
 
Ellen
 
Vogt,
 
and
 
Deborah
 
Short
 
and
 
has
 
been
 
used
 
in
 
schools
 
across
 
the
 
country
 
and
 
in
 
Maine.
 
The
 
8
 
Components
 
of
 
SIOP
 
The
 
model
 
is
 
structured
 
around
 
30
 
distinct
 
features
 
categorized
 
into
 
eight
 
core
 
planning
 
and
 
delivery
 
components:
 
 
●
 
Lesson
 
Preparation:
 
Clearly
 
define
 
and
 
post
 
content
 
and
 
language
 
objectives
 
(Learning
 
Goals
 
and
 
Language
 
Goals)
 
for
 
every
 
lesson
 
using
 
appropriate
 
supplementary
 
materials.
 
●
 
Building
 
Background:
 
Connect
 
new
 
concepts
 
directly
 
to
 
students'
 
prior
 
experiences,
 
background
 
knowledge,
 
and
 
key
 
vocabulary.
●
 
Comprehensible
 
Input:
 
Adjust
 
teacher
 
speech,
 
use
 
clear
 
modeling,
 
and
 
incorporate
 
visual
 
aids
 
or
 
gestures
 
to
 
make
 
explanations
 
understandable.
 
 
●
 
Strategies:
 
Provide
 
scaffolding,
 
support
 
higher-order
 
thinking,
 
and
 
teach
 
students
 
explicit
 
learning
 
strategies
 
to
 
foster
 
independence.
 
●
 
Interaction:
 
Create
 
frequent
 
opportunities
 
for
 
structured
 
peer-to-peer
 
and
 
student-to-teacher
 
discussions
 
to
 
practice
 
academic
 
language.
 
●
 
Practice
 
&
 
Application:
 
Provide
 
hands-on
 
activities
 
and
 
meaningful
 
group
 
tasks
 
where
 
students
 
can
 
apply
 
both
 
content
 
knowledge
 
and
 
literacy
 
skills.
 
●
 
Lesson
 
Delivery:
 
Pace
 
the
 
lesson
 
appropriately,
 
support
 
the
 
stated
 
objectives,
 
and
 
keep
 
student
 
engagement
 
high.
 
●
 
Review
 
&
 
Assessment:
 
Conduct
 
frequent
 
checks
 
for
 
understanding,
 
provide
 
regular
 
feedback,
 
and
 
review
 
key
 
vocabulary
 
and
 
content
 
objectives.
